transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (SE), Luis Ortega (SA); Mark Reynolds (Lumina - Procurement), Elena Cruz (Lumina - Legal), Derek Wu (Lumina - CTO), Priya Nair (Lumina - Security), Hannah Cole (Lumina - Platform)

Summary:
Quick procurement intake to clarify MSA/DPA points, discuss KMS key custody options for private deployments, pricing path (committed vs on-demand), and technical preflight for a short Dedicated pilot.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines and liability caps
- Data residency and audit log retention
- KMS/HSM integration and customer key custody (bring your own key)
- SLA tiers, latency SLOs, rollback/fallback policies
- Pricing structure: committed reserved capacity vs burst/hosted API mix
- Pilot scope and technical benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time. I'll do quick intros, we're Jordan Lee on the AE side, Samira and Luis from solutions.
[00:15] Mark (Procurement): Hi all, Mark here. We're trying to get clarity on a couple contract points before we route to finance.
[00:22] Elena (Legal): Elena from legal, yes, specifically liability, data handling and KMS.
[00:28] Derek (CTO): And hi, Derek. We'll cover the tech constraints, but main ask is we need KMS options and an explicit timeline for a pilot.
[00:35] Jordan: Great. Agenda for us — MSA/DPA redlines, KMS options, pricing path. Samira do you want to kick into technical notes?
[00:42] Samira (SE): Sure — high level, Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For pilot you mentioned Dedicated?
[00:51] Hannah (Platform): Yes, we prefer Dedicated for isolation, though we might start with hosted to move faster if tradeoffs allow. Dedicated gives us predictable throughput which is important.
[01:02] Luis (SA): Quick note — Dedicated pools can be configured with customer KMS, and we support external key management via KMS integration (AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM connectors). There are two patterns: envelope encryption with customer keys, or full BYOK where the key never leaves the customer's control.
[01:25] Priya (Security): When you say BYOK, do you mean keys never leave our HSM? We need FIPS 140-2 module assurances and key custody controls. Also want to know auditability of key usage.
[01:40] Samira: Yes, BYOK for Dedicated can be configured with HSM-backed KMS. Our integration logs key usage events and we can surface those in the audit trail. That said, some of the logging pipeline resides in the control plane — we can discuss an architecture where audit logs are streamed to your SIEM.
[01:58] Elena: Important for us: the DPA needs explicit language that customer data is not accessible and keys remain under customer control. Can you share sample DPA clauses?
[02:07] Jordan: Absolutely. I'll send our standard DPA and highlight the BYOK/KMS section. We also have precedent redlines from other healthcare customers we can share.
[02:15] Mark: On the MSA side, finance is pushing to cap liability at a low multiple — they're not comfortable with uncapped exposure. Is that negotiable?
[02:26] Jordan: We typically have a liability cap aligned with the contract value, some customers push for higher. For enterprise deals we can discuss exceptions but we need that routed through legal.
[02:36] Elena: We will propose a 2x revenue cap, but need also to clarify indemnity for data breaches caused by vendor negligence.
[02:46] Jordan: Noted. We'll include language examples.
[02:50] Derek: From a tech standpoint, what's the SLA latency target on Dedicated? We need tail latency guarantees under load; healthcare workflows are sensitive to 99.9th percentile latency.
[03:02] Samira: Our Dedicated SLA is configurable but our typical target is 99.9 uptime and latency SLOs depend on model and sequence length. For the pilot we can pick a model variant and lock the sequence length distribution so we can commit to a realistic p99 latency.
[03:19] Luis: Also worth considering fallback policies: if a dedicated pool is degraded we can failover to a cheaper hosted variant with different latency characteristics — that should be reflected in the SLO and rollback policy.
[03:33] Priya: That fallback is ok as long as it doesn't send data outside approved regions or change encryption characteristics.
[03:41] Samira: Good point — we can configure routing rules so the fallback stays in same region and honors BYOK — depends on capacity in that region. If fallback uses hosted multi-tenant, keys can't be customer-held in the same way; we will call that out.
[03:59] Hannah: So we need a strict separation: Dedicated + BYOK for production; hosted fallback only for non-sensitive workloads. We'll document that.
[04:09] Mark: Pricing — procurement wants committed reserved hours vs on-demand. How flexible are commited terms? We're looking at a 12-month commit but with some headroom.
[04:21] Jordan: We offer reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. Headroom/burst can be included as an add-on. We can model a blended rate: baseline committed units at lower cost, bursts billed at on-demand. We'll put an example pricing sheet.
[04:36] Elena: On billing, we need to verify egress fees and if any extra charges occur for KMS calls. Also how are logs retained and is there a charge for log egress?
[04:47] Luis: Egress for model outputs is standard; logs export to customer bucket is charged at nominal transfer rates only. KMS usage calls are typically billed by your cloud provider, not us, but if we proxy calls there may be costs. We'll document the flows and cost responsibilities.
[05:05] Derek: For the pilot, we expect about 500 requests per minute with 128 token responses average, mostly short prompts. We'll validate exact QPS with production mix later.
[05:17] Jordan: Perfect — Samira, can you note that as the benchmark target?
[05:22] Samira: Yup, we'll run a 500 QPS-ish test in a Dedicated test cluster and capture p50/p95/p99 and token costs. We'll also test batching to measure cost reductions.
[05:33] Hannah: One more on compliance — we need to map Redwood's SOC2 evidence and any FedRAMP roadmap if you have one. Healthcare customers ask for that.
[05:44] Jordan: We are SOC2 Type II — I'll share the latest report under NDA. We don't currently have FedRAMP, but we can discuss private deployment options for more regulated environments.
[05:56] Elena: If private on-prem is required, do you offer an air-gapped deployment? There are implications for telemetry and managed updates.
[06:05] Luis: We do an on-prem package — usually customers accept a private control plane with local data plane. Updates are managed via an approved channel, and audit logs can stay on-prem. That tends to be a separate commercial arrangement.
[06:20] Priya: Security — can you confirm RBAC granularity and token rotation policies? Also SSO options (SAML/SCIM)?
[06:30] Samira: RBAC supports per-team and per-route roles, token rotation via short-lived JWTs is supported, and we integrate with SAML/SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:41] Mark: On the contracting cadence, what's the fastest timeline to get to signature if legal accepts standard redlines? Procurement wants a 3-week window ideally.
[06:51] Jordan: If redlines are standard and no atypical indemnity changes, 2–3 weeks is doable. Larger liability asks or FedRAMP/private demands extend that.
[07:02] Elena: We'll draft MSA redlines and share by Friday. One topic: carveouts for data processed for model training — Lumina won't allow retention or use of PHI for model improvement. Need explicit prohibition.
[07:15] Jordan: Understood. Our standard DPA has model use clauses that can be tightened; we'll propose explicit language to disallow training on customer data for that account.
[07:25] Derek: For the Dedicated pilot, how quick to provision? We need a timeline for spin-up and a test run.
[07:33] Samira: Typically provisioning dedicated pool takes 3–5 business days once payment and networking are set. If we pre-provision and you provide networking info earlier we can accelerate.
[07:45] Hannah: Networking: we need VPC peering and egress IPs for allowlisting — can you provide a host list?
[07:54] Luis: We'll give a CIDR range and egress IPs; if you require private link-like connectivity we can do that as part of the private deployment.
[08:04] Mark: Will we get a trial invoice or credit for the pilot? Procurement needs to charge against a PO.
[08:12] Jordan: We can do a short-term invoice for pilot charges or issue a credit memo against an initial committed invoice. We'll align with your procurement process.
[08:22] Elena: A couple legal nuances — we want to keep security incident notification at 24 hours and require subprocessor lists and flow diagrams. Can you provide those?
[08:33] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a subprocessor list and network flow diagrams. Incident notification target is usually 72 hours, but for enterprise we can contractually commit to 24 hours — that's a legal negotiation point.
[08:47] Priya: 24 hours is non-negotiable for us due to regulatory posture. We'll highlight that in our redlines.
[08:55] Jordan: Noted. We'll flag that to Legal.
[09:00] Mark: On payment terms, finance prefers Net 45. Is that acceptable?
[09:08] Jordan: Standard is Net 30, but Net 45 could be approved for enterprise with procurement reasons — that may affect discounting.
[09:17] Elena: We will put Net 45 in our term sheet and discuss discounting as needed.
[09:24] Derek: Any limits on tokenization/batching that impact latencies? We've seen some systems that batch too aggressively and hurt p99.
[09:33] Samira: We have workload-aware batching — you can set a max latency budget for batching, and the runtime auto-adjusts. For latency-sensitive workloads you set a low batch timeout; for throughput-sensitive, increase the timeout. We'll provide config examples.
[09:48] Hannah: Can you share a short ops playbook for incident runbooks and failover procedures? We need that for our SRE team.
[09:56] Luis: We'll share a short ops playbook and sample runbooks for traffic spikes and failover to backup model variants.
[10:05] Mark: Let's recap concrete next steps so procurement can track.
[10:10] Jordan: Sure. Action items — Jordan to send MSA/DPA redline examples and SOC2, Samira to run Dedicated benchmark 500 rpm, Derek to share exact QPS/prompt mix, Elena to draft legal redlines including 24-hour incident notification and training prohibition. We'll add pricing examples for committed vs on-demand.
[10:27] Elena: Quick question — do you support data residency in eu-west-1 specifically? Some of our data needs to stay in EU.
[10:37] Jordan: Yes, we have EU regions on the Hosted side and can provision Dedicated pools in EU region for Private/Dedicated. We'll confirm capacity and egress implications.
[10:49] Priya: And for encryption-at-rest, can you provide the encryption algorithm and key length? We need AES-256 at minimum.
[10:56] Samira: AES-256 is standard for at-rest; KMS uses AES-GCM for envelope encryption, key lengths per cloud KMS standards. We'll include a cryptography appendix.
[11:07] Mark: Ok that's all from procurement. If we get the doc packet by Friday we can route through finance next week. Thanks.
[11:13] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll get things out this week. Any final quick clarifications?
[11:18] Derek: Just to confirm — fallback to hosted will not use BYOK and will be subject to a separate DPA clause?
[11:26] Jordan: Correct — fallback to hosted means different key handling. We'll note the behavior and ensure it's in the DPA and SLO plan.
[11:33] Elena: Thanks all.
[11:35] Jordan: Great, meeting adjourned — look out for the MSA packet and benchmark plan.
